gaps.sentence: 'I didn't take your charger,' she insisted. She ___ taking my charger.
gaps.explanation: Denials are reported as deny + -ing: denied taking.

gaps.sentence: 'Thank you for delivering it so quickly,' she said. She ___ me for delivering it so quickly.
gaps.explanation: Thanks are reported as thank somebody for + -ing.

gaps.sentence: 'I'll carry those bags for you,' he said. He ___ to carry my bags.
gaps.explanation: Offers of help are reported as offered to do something.

gaps.sentence: 'I saw him this morning,' she said on Monday afternoon. She said she had seen him ___ morning.
gaps.explanation: This morning, reported later the same day, becomes that morning.

gaps.sentence: 'The train left ten minutes ago,' she said. She said the train ___ ten minutes before.
gaps.explanation: Past simple becomes past perfect, and 'ago' becomes 'before': had left ten minutes before.

gaps.sentence: 'I really must have that report by five,' the editor said. The editor ___ on having the report by five.
gaps.explanation: Insisting on a demand: insist on + -ing (or insist that + clause).

gaps.sentence: 'Please, please don't leave me,' he sobbed. He begged her ___ leave him.
gaps.hint: beg sb not to do sth
gaps.explanation: Negative begging: begged her not to leave; the negative precedes the infinitive.

gaps.sentence: 'Well done, you've passed!' the examiner said. The examiner ___ me on passing.
